headline: Chip Stocks Pace a Broad Midday Advance as a Gas Producer Leaps
body_html:
Stocks are leaning firmly higher at midday, with 379 of the 544 names we track up and 160 down. Semiconductors lead by a wide margin, gaining 2.77%. Energy is up 1.26%, industrials 1.14% and materials 1.13%. Healthcare, consumer and software names are modestly positive. Homebuilders, down 0.11%, are the only group in the red. Prices are not final.

The standout mover is Range Resources, up 15.71%. Its natural-gas peer EQT is down 3.33%, so the jump looks specific to the company rather than a sector-wide move. Elsewhere, the strongest gains cluster in companies tied to computing and power infrastructure: Comfort Systems USA is up 8.36%, Bloom Energy 8.35%, Vicor 8.09%, Everpure 6.79% and Ciena 6.31%.

Into the close, watch whether chips hold their lead or give back gains. Fair Isaac and Arlo Technologies are each down about 8%, and solar names remain soft. Middle East headlines, including Iran diplomacy hopes and Israel's vote, could still move energy shares. Tuesday's session comes next.

briefs.headline: Semiconductors Set the Pace
briefs.body: The chip group is up 2.77% at midday, more than double the gain of any other sector we track. Energy, industrials and materials follow, each up roughly 1% to 1.3%. Only homebuilders are lower, off 0.11%.

briefs.headline: Range Resources Rockets, EQT Slips
briefs.body: Range Resources is up 15.71%, the biggest gain in our universe. Fellow gas producer EQT is down 3.33%. The split suggests investors are reacting to company-specific news rather than a group-wide move in natural gas.

briefs.headline: Infrastructure Names Lead the Gainers
briefs.body: Comfort Systems USA, Bloom Energy and Vicor are each up more than 8%. Everpure and Ciena are up about 6% to 7%. The cluster points to demand for companies supplying the hardware, cooling and power behind the computing buildout.

briefs.headline: Fair Isaac and Arlo Slide Nearly 8%
briefs.body: Fair Isaac and Arlo Technologies are the weakest names we track, each down about 7.9% at midday. National Vision is also lower, off 4.31%. All three are falling against a market where most stocks are rising.

briefs.headline: Solar Stocks Lag the Rally
briefs.body: Enphase Energy is down 3.28% and SolarEdge 2.82%, even as the wider market advances. Both rank among the session's weakest performers, leaving solar as a notable pocket of weakness in an otherwise firm tape.

briefs.headline: Gulf Markets Rebound on Diplomacy Hopes
briefs.body: Most Gulf bourses are recovering on hopes for Iran diplomacy, though Egypt is lower ahead of a vote on military support for Saudi Arabia. Those regional tensions are one reason traders may keep a close eye on energy shares into the close.
